text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock jumped 4.6% today after dropping nearly 17% over the past two weeks, driven by a bounce-back from oversold levels following crude oil's sharp decline. Brent crude fell below $90 a barrel on Monday amid optimism about Iran de-escalation, which had hammered refiner stocks—lower oil prices compress the profit margin (the difference between what refiners pay for crude and what they sell refined products for). Today's rally appears to be a technical recovery rather than a fundamental shift, as crude remains well below the $107+ levels that were supporting the stock earlier in the month.

The broader headwind for refiners remains real: even with refineries running at a healthy 94.5%, lower global oil prices and de-escalation hopes in the Middle East remove the geopolitical risk premium that had supported energy stocks. Meanwhile, political momentum is shifting toward renewable energy investments following the election outcomes, which could add long-term pressure on traditional refining demand.
